subject: Acme competitive bakeoff: plan, success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Lisa Park <lisa.park@acme.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Acme competitive bakeoff: plan, success criteria & next steps

Hi John / Lisa —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the productive discussion. Quick recap and proposed plan to get the competitive bakeoff kicked off next week. Please flag anything missing or incorrect.

Recap / qualification
- Scope: customer-facing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assistant for product support across ~2M monthly queries.
- Primary constraints: per-request p95 SLO target ~350ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens), bulk batch throughput for nightly batch jobs, and strict data controls (no retention outside VPC for private deployments).
- Baseline competitors you'd like included: AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex, and Vendor X inference API.

Redwood differentiators to test
- Prefix/KV caching to reduce repeated token cost on conversational flows
- Unified runtime that supports canary/fallback routing to cheaper quantized variants
- Transparent token-level cost breakdown and tooling for production rollout
- Private/VPC deployment and KMS-integration for regulated data

Proposed bakeoff test plan (high-level)
1) Functional accuracy: run your annotated prompt set (~200 prompts) and measure response quality and hallucination rate. (Owner: Acme provides dataset — Lisa)
2) Latency profile: p50/p95/p99 on short prompts (<=512 tokens) and long contexts (>=2k tokens). (Owner: Redwood SE — Aditya)
3) Throughput and scaling: sustained QPS test with 100 concurrent sessions and autoscaling behavior under load. (Owner: Redwood infra + Acme infra)
4) Cost comparison: measured tokens & compute cost per 1M tokens across vendors, with caching enabled/disabled. (Owner: Redwood / Acme)
5) Cold start & failure modes: measure first-request latency after idle and behavior under node failures. (Owner: Redwood)

Success criteria (proposed)
- Functional: match or exceed baseline quality on >=80% of annotated prompts
- Latency: p95 < 350ms for short prompts; p99 < 600ms for most production flows
- Throughput: sustain target QPS (TBD with Acme) with <5% error rate
- Cost: total inference cost <= 70% of baseline hyperscaler cost for equivalent config (measured across a 1M token sample)

Timeline & owners
- Dataset delivery: Acme to upload annotated prompts & sample traffic by EOD Friday (2026-07-10) — Lisa
- Pre-kickoff smoke run: Monday 2026-07-13 morning — Redwood SE (Aditya)
- Full run window: 2026-07-13 to 2026-07-24 (2 weeks) — measurement & analysis week of 7/27

Attachments: acme_bakeoff_plan_v1.xlsx (plan + checklist)

Next steps/asks
- Lisa: confirm dataset location and access method (S3 pre-signed vs. secure upload).
- John: confirm the baseline vendors you want included (Bedrock / Vertex / Vendor X) and any specific model versions.
- Aditya: can you scope the harness and confirm required access (keys, IP allowlist)?

I'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff for Monday morning to run the smoke test. Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference

From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>

Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 10:02:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme competitive bakeoff: plan, success criteria & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Dataset: we'll upload a tarball with 200 annotated prompts + 10k production-sampled logs. We'll need guidance on safe redaction for PII; can you confirm Redwood's recommended redaction steps?
- Success criteria: the quality metric is fine, but can you add a more prescriptive definition for "match or exceed" — e.g., >=0.05 improvement in BLEU/F1 or equivalent human-annotated preference rate?
- Hyperscaler baseline: yes, please include Bedrock (gpt-4o-family if possible) and Vertex (PaLM family). Vendor X is optional but would like a single-run for comparison.

Also — can Aditya share the exact endpoint URLs, expected request payload shape, and a sample curl command so our infra can pre-authorize traffic and IP ranges?

I'll confirm a Monday time after checking with the SRE team. Looking forward to the kickoff.

John
Head of Product — Search & Support
Acme Corp

Hi John / Marissa —

Following up with a more technical scope for the bakeoff and what I'll deliver before Monday's smoke test: 

Deliverables
- Pre-configured test harness (GitHub repo link) with load scripts (wrk/locust based) and a data loader for the annotated prompts.
- Endpoint templates & sample requests (curl + python snippets) for the Redwood hosted endpoint and private deployment.
- Collection artifacts: latency histograms (per-model per-run), token counts, GPU utilization logs, and a standardized CSV with per-prompt judgmentables.

Test config details
- Models / variants: rwd-lambda-1.0 (fp16), rwd-lambda-1.0-quant (int8), plus the same sized baseline model on Bedrock/Vertex for parity runs.
- Tokenization: use shared tokenizer; we'll provide a script to normalize token counts for cross-vendor cost apples-to-apples.
- Concurrency: smoke run at 10 concurrent sessions; full throughput sweep 10 -> 100 -> 500 concurrent sessions (as agreed).
- Request payload: JSON with {"prompt":..., "user_id":..., "session_id":..., "max_tokens":..., "temperature":...}.

Reproducibility/runbook
- We'll checkpoint model and harness versions in the repo and tag the run metadata.
- I'll provide a short runbook to reproduce results locally and in your staging account.

Attachments: redwood_bakeoff-checklist.pdf (checklist + runbook)

Access needs
- A service account key or an IP allowlist window for the smoke test so we can hit your staging endpoint.
- If you prefer, we can run against a Redwood-managed private env and provide results without direct access (needs sign-off).

I'll drop the harness link and the curl snippets by EOD Sunday. Happy to jump on a quick call if your SRE wants to walk through the IP/key details.

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
